arguments.summary: Completed-session technical snapshot through 2026-09-18 (split-adjusted SIP price-return basis): META shows the strongest 21/63-session momentum and relative performance; ANET is also positive on both horizons. NVDA is constructive but modest at 21 sessions. MU has strong 21-session recovery but remains negative over 63 sessions and has the highest realized volatility. QQQ is above its key moving averages but its 63-session return and relative performance are negative. These are descriptive observations, not return forecasts.

claims.text: ANET closed at $199.39, above its 20-, 50-, and 200-session SMAs; its completed 21- and 63-session price returns were 6.94% and 17.52%, respectively. Its annualized realized volatility was 45.00% (21 sessions) and 57.14% (63 sessions), and it was 5.28% below its 252-session-window high.
ANET exceeded SPY by 7.90 percentage points over 21 sessions and 15.51 points over 63 sessions; it exceeded XLK by 3.69 and 18.48 points, respectively, on compatible 2026-09-18 price-return inputs.

QQQ closed at $721.45, above its 20-, 50-, and 200-session SMAs. Its 21-session return was 0.75%, but its 63-session return was -2.59%; realized volatility was 13.19% and 20.85%, respectively, and drawdown from the 252-session-window high was 3.31%.

QQQ exceeded SPY by 1.71 percentage points over 21 sessions but lagged SPY by 4.59 points over 63 sessions; it lagged XLK on both horizons. The supplied QQQ holding table, dated 2026-09-12 and marked stale, lists NVDA at 8.45%, MU at 4.85%, and META at 3.07%.

MU closed at $1,015.80, above its 20-, 50-, and 200-session SMAs. It returned 8.40% over 21 sessions but -10.42% over 63 sessions, with realized volatility of 52.49% and 89.56%; it was 16.30% below its 252-session-window high.
MU outperformed SPY and XLK over 21 sessions by 9.36 and 5.15 percentage points, respectively, but lagged them over 63 sessions by 12.42 and 9.46 points.

META closed at $665.75, above its 20-, 50-, and 200-session SMAs. Its 21- and 63-session returns were 21.93% and 15.34%, with realized volatility of 29.31% and 44.80%; it was 14.67% below its 252-session-window high. RSI14 was 77.87, a descriptive momentum reading rather than a reversal signal.
META exceeded SPY by 22.88 percentage points over 21 sessions and 13.34 points over 63 sessions; versus XLC, the excess was 22.38 and 14.09 points.

NVDA closed at $222.27, above its 20-, 50-, and 200-session SMAs. Its 21- and 63-session returns were 2.16% and 5.50%, with realized volatility of 44.72% and 39.63%; it was 5.71% below its 252-session-window high.
NVDA exceeded SPY by 3.12 percentage points over 21 sessions and 3.49 points over 63 sessions; it lagged XLK by 1.08 points over 21 sessions but exceeded it by 6.46 points over 63 sessions.

The price backdrop is mixed rather than uniformly risk-on: SPY was essentially flat over 21 sessions and up 2.00% over 63, while XLK was positive over 21 sessions but slightly negative over 63. Thus, the positive relative results in ANET and META are not simply broad-SPY strength; this is relative-performance context, not causal attribution.

gaps.description: Daily summary fields do not provide dated prior swing highs/lows, volume/liquidity measures, or full bar paths; therefore no chart-pattern support/resistance, volume confirmation, or event-to-price causality is asserted.
QQQ holdings data are dated 2026-09-12 and explicitly marked stale; its look-through weights are contextual only and should be refreshed before exposure-specific conclusions.

assumptions: All price comparisons use compatible 2026-09-18 split-adjusted SIP daily price-return fields.
Realized volatility is historical annualized dispersion and is not an implied distribution or forecast.
Moving-average levels are used only as auditable review triggers, not as intrinsic value or trading instructions.
arguments.counter_thesis: Prices above moving averages and recent relative strength can fail without warning; MU's negative 63-session return and high realized volatility, META's elevated RSI reading, and QQQ's 63-session underperformance show that the technical observations do not establish persistent momentum.

review_conditions.description: Review ANET's 21/63-session momentum thesis if a completed split-adjusted close is below its current 20-session SMA reference.

Review MU's recovery interpretation if a completed split-adjusted close is below its current 20-session SMA reference, especially given its high realized volatility and still-negative 63-session return.
Review META's extended-momentum interpretation if a completed split-adjusted close is below its current 20-session SMA reference.
Review NVDA's constructive trend interpretation if a completed split-adjusted close is below its current 20-session SMA reference.
Review QQQ's above-moving-average posture if a completed split-adjusted close is below its current 50-session SMA reference; its 63-session relative performance is already negative.

shared_exposures.mechanism: The dated QQQ holding table identifies direct look-through positions in NVDA, MU and META, so company-specific moves can overlap with QQQ exposure. Reported weights are stale and ANET is not evidenced as a QQQ holding in this table; no portfolio allocation inference follows.
shared_exposures.qualification: Composition is as of 2026-09-12, marked stale, and historical composition is not established.
